name: NCBIDatasets_get_gene
description: Get comprehensive gene information from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) by Gene ID. Returns gene symbol, description, chromosomal location, genomic coordinates, cross-references to UniProt/Ensembl/OMIM, synonyms, and annotation details. Covers all organisms in the NCBI Gene database. No API key is required; optionally set NCBI_API_KEY for a higher request-rate limit. Example: gene_id 7157 returns TP53 (tumor protein p53) on chromosome 17.

gene_ontology.description: GO annotations on the record, dropped whole before: TP53 carries 122 biological processes, each with the GO id, the evidence code, the qualifier (acts_upstream_of_or_within is not involved_in) and the PMIDs it was asserted from.

summary.description: RefSeq's own paragraph on what the gene does; `description` is "tumor protein p53"

annotation_releases.description: Which annotation release the coordinates come from, with its accession and release date -- what makes a coordinate reproducible

reference_standards.description: The RefSeqGene record, the stable coordinate system clinical variant nomenclature is written against

name: NCBIDatasets_get_gene_by_symbol
description: Look up gene information by gene symbol and organism. Searches NCBI Gene database using official gene symbols. Specify the species with `taxon` (or its synonyms `organism`/`species`) as a common name (human, mouse, rat) or taxonomy ID. IMPORTANT -- the species defaults to HUMAN when none is given, so a gene symbol shared across species returns the human gene unless you say otherwise; `metadata.query_taxon_defaulted` is true whenever that default was applied, and `metadata.query_taxon` echoes the species actually used. Every returned row also carries its own `tax_id`/`taxname`, which is the authoritative check. Returns gene ID, description, chromosomal location, and database cross-references.

taxon.description: Organism as common name or taxonomy ID. Examples: 'human', 'mouse', 'rat', '9606', '10090'. Default: 'human' (reported as metadata.query_taxon_defaulted). Synonyms `organism` and `species` are accepted.

organism.description: Synonym for `taxon`. Used when `taxon` is not supplied.

species.description: Synonym for `taxon`. Used when neither `taxon` nor `organism` is supplied.

gene_ontology.description: GO annotations for the gene, split by aspect

assigned_by.description: Which group assigned the annotations, e.g. GOA

evidence_code.description: GO evidence code, e.g. IDA or IEA: the difference between an experimentally supported annotation and an electronically inferred one

qualifier.description: Qualifier such as NOT or contributes_to, which can invert the annotation's meaning

evidence_code.description: GO evidence code, e.g. IDA or IEA: the difference between an experimentally supported annotation and an electronically inferred one

qualifier.description: Qualifier such as NOT or contributes_to, which can invert the annotation's meaning

evidence_code.description: GO evidence code, e.g. IDA or IEA: the difference between an experimentally supported annotation and an electronically inferred one

qualifier.description: Qualifier such as NOT or contributes_to, which can invert the annotation's meaning

summary.description: Descriptive summaries, each with its source

annotation_releases.description: Which annotation releases the gene appears in

reference_standards.description: Curated reference sequence ranges for the gene

gene_range.description: The RefSeqGene range, with its accession and coordinates

gene_groups.description: Gene group memberships, each with the method that assigned it

map_locations.description: Map positions, e.g. the cytogenetic band

nomenclature_authority.description: The naming authority for the symbol and its identifier there

identifier.description: Identifier at that authority, e.g. HGNC:1100

genomic_locations.description: Where the gene sits on each assembly

name: NCBIDatasets_get_orthologs
description: Get orthologous genes across species for a given NCBI Gene ID. NCBI's ortholog endpoint returns a complete set rather than honoring page_size, so this tool paginates that set locally and reports the exact total, has_more, and next_offset. Returns gene symbols, species, and gene types. Example: gene_id 7157 (TP53) currently has hundreds of cross-species ortholog records.

page_size.description: Maximum orthologs in this local result page (1-1000, default 20).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the complete ortholog set (default 0). Use metadata.next_offset to continue.

gene_ontology_counts.description: GO term counts per aspect. An orthologs page answers the same full gene records as the single-gene tool -- 2,622 GO terms across one page -- so the counts are here and the terms are in NCBIDatasets_get_gene.

name: NCBIDatasets_get_taxonomy
description: Get detailed taxonomy information from NCBI by taxonomy ID. Returns organism name, rank, full lineage (as bare ancestor tax_ids in `lineage`, and as resolved organism_name/rank pairs in `lineage_names`), current counts of genes/assemblies/RNA types, and child taxa. Covers all organisms in NCBI Taxonomy including bacteria, archaea, eukaryotes, and viruses. Example: tax_id 9606 returns Homo sapiens and its root-to-parent lineage.

tax_id.description: NCBI Taxonomy ID (numeric). Examples: '9606' (Homo sapiens), '10090' (Mus musculus), '7227' (Drosophila melanogaster), '562' (E. coli).

lineage_names.description: Ancestor tax_ids from `lineage`, resolved to organism_name/rank (root-first). Entries fall back to null names/ranks if the resolution lookup failed.

genetic_code.description: Which translation tables apply: 1/Standard for the nuclear genome and 2/Vertebrate Mitochondrial for the mitochondrion. Reading a mitochondrial ORF with the standard code gives the wrong protein.

scientific_name_authority.description: The authority that published the name, which in taxonomy is part of the name

name: NCBIDatasets_suggest_taxonomy
description: Suggest taxonomic names matching a query string. Searches NCBI Taxonomy for organisms by partial name, returning matching scientific names, taxonomy IDs, common names, and ranks. Useful for finding taxonomy IDs from partial organism names. Example: 'drosophila' returns D. melanogaster (7227), D. simulans (7240), etc.

query.description: Partial organism name to search. Examples: 'drosophila', 'escherichia', 'arabidopsis', 'saccharomyces'.

name: NCBIDatasets_get_genome_assembly
description: Get genome assembly metadata for an assembly accession (RefSeq GCF_ or GenBank GCA_) from the NCBI Datasets v2 API. Returns organism/strain, assembly name/level/status, RefSeq category (e.g. reference genome), release date, submitter, BioProject, and assembly statistics (total length, chromosome count, contig/scaffold N50, GC%, annotation provider). Use to characterize a specific genome assembly across any organism (bacteria, fungi, plant, animal). No API key required.

accession.description: Assembly accession, e.g. 'GCF_000005845.2' (E. coli K-12) or 'GCF_000001405.40' (human GRCh38.p14).

oneOf.description: Curated assembly fields (accession, organism, level, stats)

name: NCBIDatasets_list_genomes_by_taxon
description: List genome assemblies available for a taxon (NCBI tax id or scientific name) via the NCBI Datasets v2 API. Returns assembly summaries, the exact total count available, and continuation metadata. When metadata.has_more is true, pass metadata.next_page_token back as page_token to retrieve the next page. Set reference_only to restrict to reference/representative genomes. No API key required.

taxon.description: NCBI tax id or scientific name, e.g. '562', 'Escherichia coli', 'Saccharomyces cerevisiae'.

limit.description: Assemblies per page (default 20, maximum reliable upstream size 1000).

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token from metadata.next_page_token. Omit for the first page.

reference_only.description: If true, return only reference/representative genomes.

name: NCBIDatasets_get_sequence_reports
description: Get a page of per-sequence (chromosome/plasmid/scaffold) reports for a genome assembly via the NCBI Datasets v2 API. Returns each molecule's chromosome name, role, location type, RefSeq and GenBank accessions, length, and GC%, plus total_available and next_page_token metadata. Use next_page_token to retrieve additional pages for assemblies with many sequences. Use to map an assembly to its individual sequence accessions (e.g. resolve E. coli K-12 to NC_000913.3, or human chromosomes to their RefSeq NC_ accessions). No API key required.

page_size.description: Maximum sequence records in this page (default 100, maximum 1000).

page_token.description: Opaque next_page_token returned by a previous call. Omit for the first page.
